record.original_question: Which conditional independence models can actually be realized by multivariate Gaussian distributions on R^n? Equivalently, how can one study the geometry of Gaussian conditional independence models, that is, semi-algebraic subsets of the cone PD_n of positive definite symmetric n×n matrices defined by equations of the form [i ⊥⊥ j | K] = 0?

evidence.quote: The general question behind this asks for characterization of all conditional independence models which can be realized by Gaussians on R^n.
General Problem: Study the geometry of conditional independence models for multivariate Gaussian random variables.
A Gaussian conditional independence model, or GCI model for short, is any semi-algebraic subset of the cone PDn which can be defined by polynomial equations of the form [i⊥⊥ j |K ] = 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{PD}_n$ denote the cone of real symmetric positive definite $n\times n$ matrices, identified with the parameter space of centered nondegenerate Gaussian distributions on $\mathbb{R}^n$ via their covariance matrices $\Sigma=(\sigma_{ij})$. For a Gaussian random vector $X=(X_1,\dots,X_n)$ with covariance $\Sigma$, indices $i\neq j\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, and a subset $K\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}\setminus\{i,j\}$, the conditional independence statement $X_i\perp\!\!\!\perp X_j\mid X_K$ holds if and only if the $(|K|+1)\times(|K|+1)$ subdeterminant
$$[i\perp\!\!\!\perp j\mid K](\Sigma)\;:=\;\det\Sigma_{(\{i\}\cup K),\,(\{j\}\cup K)}\;=\;0.$$
Define a Gaussian conditional independence (GCI) model to be any semi-algebraic subset of $\mathrm{PD}_n$ that can be defined by a finite collection of polynomial equations of the form $[i\perp\!\!\!\perp j\mid K]=0$.

Problem: Develop a characterization of all conditional independence models on $n$ random variables that are realizable by some multivariate Gaussian distribution on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and study the geometry (irreducible decomposition, dimension, smoothness, singular locus) of GCI models as semi-algebraic subsets of $\mathrm{PD}_n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is an active research program in algebraic statistics. Substantial progress has been made: Sullivant and collaborators studied the algebraic geometry of Gaussian CI ideals; Drton and Xiao established smoothness results for many GCI models; and Šimeček proved that the class of Gaussian-representable CI structures admits no finite complete axiomatic characterization, ruling out a finite-rule characterization. A complete characterization of realizable Gaussian CI models remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Gaussian conditional independence relations have no finite complete characterization
status_evidence.snippet: The class of CI structures induced by regular Gaussian distributions has no finite complete characterization.
status_evidence.claim: No finite axiomatic characterization exists for Gaussian-representable CI models, showing the general realizability question has a negative answer in axiomatic form.

status_evidence.title: Smoothness of Gaussian conditional independence models
status_evidence.snippet: Studies whether GCI models contain singularities, with results for models on up to four variables.
status_evidence.claim: Geometric/smoothness aspects of GCI models have been partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Gaussian Graphical Models: An Algebraic and Geometric Perspective
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of algebraic geometry of Gaussian graphical and CI models.
status_evidence.claim: The geometry program is ongoing and substantial partial results exist.
